thread:
Maya (PM): Drafting a quick mock — thinking about exposing 'burst quanta' instead of just a toggle. Link: https://internal.redwood.design/mockups/autoscale-burst-v3.png thoughts?

Jon (Design): Love the idea. 'Burst quanta' name might confuse folks. Could be 'burst units' or 'burst capacity'? @Maya what do you think? :thinking_face: 

Maya (PM): Hmm. 'Burst capacity' maps better to mental model, but product needs discrete billing buckets so we can charge per quantum. Leaning to 'burst units' for clarity.

Ben (Product Designer): UX suggestion: show min/max as compact steppers in one row, then a separate 'Burst' slider with a tooltip: "Temporary extra GPUs for traffic spikes (charged per unit)." Keep the unit label visible next to the number.

Sasha (Eng): Backend note: API exposes integer `burst_quanta` (1..10). Slider needs snap-to-integer and show derived GPU count = base + burst_quanta * burst_size. Example config we store:
```json
{
  "min": 2,
  "max": 8,
  "burst_quanta": 2
}
```
This helps front-end compute preview.

Maya (PM): Good. Default `burst_size` should be 1 GPU and the label should say "Burst size (GPUs)". Also we need pool chooser — current mock uses a dropdown with inline tags (A100, RTX6000, Spot).

Jon (Design): Dropdown with tag icons is getting cluttered. Suggest split: primary pool selector (single select), and a horizontal row of tag chips below for extra filters (multi-select). Chips should be keyboard navigable.

Izzy (Accessibility): Strong +1 on keyboard focus. Chips need `role="option"`/aria-selected and the chip group should be a `listbox`. Also ensure selected chip color meets 4.5:1 contrast. If using brand purple, check contrast or add a visible patterned outline.

Ben (Product Designer): Copy tweak for the SLO slider: instead of generic "Latency", use "Target P99 latency (ms)" and tooltip: "Lower = faster, may increase cost and reduce throughput."

Sasha (Eng): For guardrails, can we surface an inline block if min > max or if min > some pool capacity? We'll need microcopy explaining why the change is blocked. Also add auto-fix suggestions (button: "Adjust max to X").

Maya (PM): Draft microcopy: "Minimum cannot exceed maximum. Reduce the minimum or increase the maximum to continue." Open to wording edits.

Jon (Design): That reads a bit clinical. Suggest: "This configuration isn't valid yet. Make the minimum smaller or increase the maximum to proceed." Shorter and user-friendly.

Izzy (Accessibility): Also surface errors with `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers announce changes. Buttons need `aria-describedby` linking to the error text when present.

Maya (PM): Can we add an estimated cost delta line under the controls? e.g., "Estimated cost: +$0.45/hr if burst enabled." Helps PMs decide.

Sasha (Eng): We can approximate client-side if we have per-pool unit prices. Will add API to return `unit_price_per_gpu` so front-end can calc: `delta = burst_quanta * unit_price_per_gpu`.

Ben (Product Designer): Visual: small cost chip with an info icon that opens a breakdown modal. Keep it subtle (not primary CTA).

Jon (Design): One more nit: steppers and slider thumbs need a clear, persistent focus ring (3px brand purple) for keyboard users. Also ensure thumbs have a 44px touch target on mobile.

Maya (PM): OK next steps: Jon to update mock with split pool selector + chips, Ben to draft 3 copy variants for microcopy and tooltips, Izzy to run quick a11y pass on the new components, Sasha to verify snap + cost calc, and I'll update the spec doc.

redwood-deploy-bot: Screenshot uploaded: s3://redwood-mockups/autoscale-burst-v3.png

Maya (PM): Thanks all. If we still have unresolved items let's sync Wed 10am.
